_meta.description: Known centralised-exchange deposit/hot wallets on Ethereum mainnet. A match against one of these is what lets TraceChain say 'the funds were cashed out here'.
_meta.provenance: Addresses originate from Etherscan's own public address labels (etherscan.io/accounts/label/*). The initial set was transcribed by hand; the remainder was imported from brianleect/etherscan-labels @ 923aba72c7e2d0682f7ae6194b6140bd90668dc9, a published scrape of those same pages, via backend/scripts/import_exchange_labels.py.
_meta.verification_note: Every address was checked against live mainnet data before being added: each has a real history of value-bearing transfers, consistent with exchange operation. That confirms the address is real and economically active -- it does NOT independently re-confirm which company operates it, and no free API exposes Etherscan's label data. Re-verify on etherscan.io before any evidentiary use. Candidates whose entire history was zero-value address-poisoning spam were rejected.
_meta.schema: labels maps a lowercase address to either a plain exchange name or an object {exchange, label, type}
_meta.contract_audit: Every address was checked for contract bytecode. Token contracts, DEX routers and bridges were removed -- funds reaching those have not been cashed out at an exchange. Exchange-operated contract wallets (multisig, deposit forwarders) were kept and typed 'contract_wallet'. Re-run with backend/scripts/audit_label_contracts.py.

_unverified_pending._note: Indian exchanges (WazirX, CoinDCX, ZebPay) are directly relevant to the MHA problem statement, but their hot-wallet addresses could not be sourced to a confidence level appropriate for an attribution tool. Do NOT guess them -- a wrong address produces a false attribution against a named company. Look each one up on etherscan.io/accounts/label/, confirm the label, and move the entry into 'labels' above. See README section 'Adding exchange labels'.
